Years have passed since the Great Extinction. Flora fell as autumn leaves fall, yellowed and crumbling, and what rose from the dust was not Flora at all. These new creatures, the Chlora, were taller, faster, smarter. They had the blessings of their mother-god, and the knowledge of the past at their fingertips. They were destined for greatness.

But what of their predecessors?

The Extinction forever barred the Flora from their homeland, the Tree of Life. But it did not quell them completely.

There are a few versions of what happened next.

Some say that the Flora have turned from their peaceful ways, and were punished - that in their grief many laid down and died, to mirror the passing of their brothers at the Tree. There is some truth to this. Many did, indeed, die of sorrow. Those that know this version of events, are the Regretful. Their color is the silver of a crying star. A Floran sect that embraces a primary truth: That without the Tree, the Flora are nothing.

Since the Extinction, much knowledge was lost: Not all even properly know what the tree is, or where it is, or if it is real at all or a metaphysical construct, an afterlife for the faithful. But all know that they may never return to the north and center, to the heart of the world. The Regretful grow their own tree. All their genius they pour into the growing of a great tree. Blasphemy? Homage? Opinions differ.

Some say the Flora have been let into the world, to grow and prosper, that Yuna the Goddess took mercy on them and set them free from her guardians, their comfortable lives, their coddling. In such an environment, Flora could not achieve the greatness they were meant for, and so the Goddess let them loose, and cut all former ties. In the ensuing struggle to survive and prosper away from their comfortable homes, many Flora died, backs bent and wooden-bones broken, that the survivors may grow stronger in the fertile soil of their passing. There is some truth to this. Many did, indeed, die as a sacrifice to the survivors. Those that know this version of events, are the Valiant. Their color is the deep green of a verdant branch. A Floran sect that embraces a primary truth: That without the Tree, the Flora may finally become great.

Since the extinction, much knowledge was gained: Techniques of agriculture, that the Flora never before had to develop in their times of bounty, led them to stability, although far less comfort and plenty than in that golden age. Military advances, that the Flora never before needed, defended them from all manner of beasts and rivals, although far more imperfectly than the indomitable god-given defenses of that golden age. The Machines of the Flora Geniuses became, of necessity, less wistful, less whimsical, and more practical. Plows, ballistae, construction equipment, refining gear. Survival and progress. These are the goals of the Valiant.

Some say the Flora have been tasked with spreading the Pattern of the Tree, learned in its great reflective pools, across the lands, and in this task, they have failed. The Pattern was torn from them, and without the vital presence of the Pattern, a great calamity rained down from the skies. Striving to atone, to regain this greatest art, to lead the world to its rightful path, many Florans went mad and died. There is some truth to this. Many did, indeed, die of madness, trying to understand what happened and failing. Those that know this version of events, are the Besotted. Their color is the blue-and-purple of a delicate flower. A Floran sect that embraces a primary truth: That without the Flora, the Tree - nay, the world - is doomed, and without purpose.

Since the Extinction, much knowledge was preserved: The basic shapes of the Pattern. The legends of the Guardian Fruit. The locations of lost outposts and old allies. the Flora were great once, and nearly straddled the world. The Besotted seek to guard, recover, use this knowledge - for the ultimate goal, a return to the great task: The Spreading of the Pattern. They have yet some original scrolls of the Perfect Pattern, that must be heavily guarded, for each replication of it is for some reason less and less perfect, devolving into useless squares after enough iterations. They have collections of odd plants and strange chemicals, obtained by ancient promises redeemed. Even now they seek to re-create the Guardian Fruit. Experiments are, so far, hardly, ah, fruitful, and many devoted Florans die a mutant, twisting, horrible death in the attempt.

There are many such sects. The Pale seek to unite the sects and tribes, and especially to reconnect with the Heavy, a lost tribe of Flora that live in the Heavy Places. The Dejected reject their old Goddess who betrayed them, and seek to distance themselves from their past by traveling in the Fleshwinds intentionally, becoming mutant and strange. The Lost seek refuge among other races, and see themselves as inferior to those not so God-cursed as they, prizing servitude to their betters above all else. The Open are obsessed with the Chrlora, and would seek their guidance and blessings, would seek to emulate them in all things. The Clement are obsessed with Chlora, and would destroy and dissect them, to end this abomination. Others exist.

From all these divergent schools of thought, one notion resounds and echoes from every throat:

The Flora live, despite their near-Extinction.

The Flora yet live.
